basis: Blood-vessel endothelial malignancy; cutaneous tumors directly occupy skin in roughly 50% across the umbrella. Other anatomical sites are less frequent.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous origin accounts for roughly half of cases, exceeding 30%; variable tumor sites do not exclude this common site.

basis: Digestive-system tumor origin defines this umbrella; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease. Pancreatic endocrine tumors are a subset.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: neuroendocrine differentiation is not itself endocrine-gland disease; this umbrella also includes nonfunctional digestive carcinomas.

basis: Defining encephalopathy; retinal dysfunction 17/22, liver disease with hepatomegaly 32/73. Cap omits hearing loss 29/64, renal cysts 4/12 and skeletal stippling 12/12.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neonatal seizures and profound developmental impairment define the disease; developmental delay affects 126/126 and seizures 79/85.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental impairment; dental abnormalities 30-79%, pes planus 2/4. Obesity 3/5 alone does not establish direct endocrine injury; major eye and heart defects are occasional.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity in 3/5 alone does not demonstrate direct endocrine-gland damage or an intrinsic metabolic defect.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural pes planus occurs in 2/4 (50%); hypotonia alone would not establish primary muscle damage.

basis: GM2 storage with defining neurodegeneration; progressive retinal ganglion-cell injury and visual loss commonly affect >30% in the severe infantile course, beyond cherry-red deposits alone.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal ganglion-cell degeneration with progressive visual loss commonly exceeds 30% in the usual severe infantile course; not based on cherry-red spots alone.

basis: Large abdominal-wall defect with congenital bowel herniation; pulmonary hypoplasia affects roughly 30-50% of giant cases. Liver herniation alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia directly impairs lung development in roughly 30-50% of giant omphaloceles, independent of treatment.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: congenital extra-abdominal herniation of bowel is part of the defining abdominal-wall/bowel malformation; primary localization does not require bowel necrosis.

basis: Extranodal B-cell lymphoma; GI tumor occupation occurs in ~40-50%. Supplied HPO pulmonary infiltrates 80-99% support lung involvement, though that frequency is atypical for the umbrella.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: supplied HPO explicitly reports pulmonary infiltrates at 80-99%; lung is a recognized site of direct lymphoma infiltration. Frequency is atypical across all MALT lymphomas.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: GI occupation affects roughly 40-50%; the umbrella is defined by extranodal lymphoid origin, with GI involvement common but not required.

basis: Mandibulofacial dysostosis, ear/hearing defects and characteristic lower-eyelid defects define TCS; cleft palate affects 4/13 (~31%), supporting gastrointestinal involvement.

decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic lower-eyelid coloboma/notching is a major defining TCS feature; coloboma is documented in 3/8, beyond cosmetic fissure slant.

basis: Benign lymphatic lesion arising in the colon. Lymphatic origin alone does not establish disease of the heart or blood vessels covered by cardiovascular.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: the lesion involves colonic lymphatic channels, not cardiac tissue or blood vessels; a broad vascular-neoplasm ancestor does not establish this axis.

basis: Recurrent alveolar hemorrhage and iron-deficiency anemia form the defining clinical triad with infiltrates; anemia affects 80-99%. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not show hepatic damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: iron-deficiency anemia is a major diagnostic feature of idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis and occurs in 80-99%; diagnostic criteria qualify despite blood-loss causation.
